ms.report:
Milestone 1: Distributed Kubernetes Operator
Milestone Outputs:
Develop open-source Kubernetes operator to handle Frontend workloads:
・An open-source Kubernetes operator has been successfully developed to manage frontend workloads. The codebase is available in a publicly accessible repository, ensuring transparency and collaboration.

Integrate operator with distributed consensus mechanism:
・The operator has been seamlessly integrated with a distributed consensus mechanism, allowing multiple clusters to interact with each other. The consensus logic can be found in the Daemon component.

Provision a 2-party staging environment with fake workloads:
・A two-party staging environment has been provisioned successfully, incorporating simulated workloads. This environment serves as a controlled testing ground to validate the operator's functionality and assess its performance under various conditions. Both environments are currently running in AWS but using different administration accounts and located in different geographic locations (US and EU).

Integrate DNS component for awareness of global topology:
・To provide a unified global topology that is accessible via DNS, each cluster is being augmented with a CloudFare tunnel. This allows us to configure a CloudFare load-balancing mechanism that resolves wildcard subdomain for a particular DNS zone (in this case, *.fabric.demeter.run). Each cluster handles an independent set of replicas for the same frontend but to the end-user it shows as a single consistent view.

Integrate reverse-proxy component for awareness of global topology:
・Each cluster contains its own reverse proxy mechanism by leveraging Kong ingress-controller for Kuberentes. This reverse proxy receives and processes inbound HTTP requests from the CloudFare tunnel and routes each one to the corresponding pod using common Kubernetes machinery.

ms.report:
Milestone Outputs:
Develop credit bookkeeping component
A credit bookkeeping system has been developed and integrated with the existing daemon component that runs on each cluster. This component monitors the Cardano blockchain for token deposits to specific customer-specific script addresses. These deposits represent payments from customers to sustain operations of the service.
This component will also monitor withdrawal transactions from infrastructure providers that represent the final settlement for the rendered services.
Develop usage-tracking bookkeeping component
A usage tracking component has been developed and integrated with the existing daemon component that runs in each cluster. This component monitors HTTP requests and records the amount of consumed credits in a ledger shared with each cluster provider.
Update 2-party staging environment
The 2-party staging environment that was delivered on the previous milestone has been updated with the latest release of the server-side components. This update allows us to test the new load-balancing mechanisms, the usage-tracking and the bookkeeping components.
Perform long-running operation tests with fake requests
We have configured an automated load testing agent using the Locust framework. This test spawns concurrent agents that execute artificial HTTP requests to our main load-balancer entry point and measures failures and latency across many attempts throughout extended periods of time. The reports of these tests are available as part of the milestone completion evidence.
Acceptance Criteria:
The 1st acceptance criteria for this milestone is having a distributed load balancer mechanism, verified for long-running operations in a two-party staging environment. We have accomplished the goal by connecting two Demeter clusters, one in the US region and another one in the EU region, through a CloudFlare tunnel that load-balances requests using a round-robin mechanism. ms.criteria: An working CI pipeline process for building frontend artifacts that it’s validated through integration tests.
ms.report:
Milestone Outputs:
Integrate an automated CI pipeline for Frontend builds
We have developed several artifacts that, when used together, provide a mechanism for executing CI build pipelines for frontends to be published to Demeter.
The main artifact is Demeter’s CLI (command line interface) which now provides a new deploy command that packages the distributable files of a frontend project into an OCI image and then pushes the image to a remote registry.
A complementary artifact is a new custom Github action that can be used in any Github workflow that installs Demeter’s CLI into the runners contexts, allowing other steps in the pipeline to execute Demeter commands, such as the new deploy command.
The final artifact is a Github workflow template that is shown as part of the Demeter’s console that devs can use to copy & paste and then customize for their needs. This workflow template will take care of building the frontend and publishing the final distributable package to Demeter.

Update the distributed staging environment to support build jobs
The 2-party staging environment that was delivered on the previous milestone has been updated with the latest release of the server-side components. This update allows us to use the build outputs from the new CI pipelines.
These changes impact both the US cluster (us-east-1) and the EU cluster (eu-central-1).
Perform integration testing focusing on build pipelines
We have created a new repository that holds a full end-to-end example of a frontend that builds and publishes to Demeter using the new build pipeline developed for this milestone.
This repository has an instance of the workflow generated from the same template that is shared to developers through Demeter’s console. It is configured to trigger on each push to the main branch and it includes all the steps up to the OCI image push.
We currently use this repository as an example but also as our source for integration testing.

Develop an API to execute RPC to request builds & deployments
Develop a CLI application to interact with the API

ms.criteria: A working, developer-friendly toolchain for deploying frontends that has been validated through integration tests.
ms.report:
Milestone Outputs:
An API to execute RPC to request builds & deployments: we’ve developed an RPC using Rust and gRPC technologies that provides programmatic access to Demeter functionality, including the endpoints responsible for packaging and deploying frontend sites that can be hosted on Demeter.
A CLI application to interact with the API: we’ve developed a command-line interface that allows developers to interact with Demeter RPC endpoints using the terminal. This component includes a feature to package local artifacts from a frontend codebase into a Docker image that can be pushed to any OCI-compatible registry.
Binaries release and end-user documentation for the CLI: we’ve released the CLI binaries for any developer to download and install. We’ve also published online documentation providing instructions on how to use Demeter’s CLI.
Acceptance Criteria:
The outputs of this milestone provide a working, developer-friendly toolchain for deploying frontends. By leveraging a client-side component (Demeter’s CLI) and a server-side component (Demeter’s RPC) developers can package their frontends as Docker images and publish them to Demeter’s hosting infrastructure.
Evidence of Milestone Completion:
Source code for an API for RPC execution and a CLI application.
・https://github.com/demeter-run/daemon/tree/main/src/drivers 
・https://github.com/demeter-run/cli/tree/main/src

・https://github.com/demeter-run/cli/releases/tag/v1.1.0 

End-user documentation site showing how to install and initialize the Demeter CLI:
・https://docs.demeter.run/cli 

Tutorial video on how to use Demeter CLI and RPC server to deploy a new frontend:
https://youtu.be/Hw9fMDkXHmY
